newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market slow at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets remained slow Friday at $72.00 per cwt, unchanged from Thursday's active sales late and steady with last week's top price, feedlot sources said.
Feedlot cattle owners next week were seen pricing cattle at $74.00 to $75.00, with sales expected at $73.00, the feedlot sources said.

Sales after midday Friday totaled about 8,500 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma regions and about 4,000 head in Kansas, the sources said. Several loads sold Friday were expected to be picked up on Monday.
Feedlot cattle price strength next week was expected to come from tight supplies of finished cattle and ideas that beef demand would be stronger next week.

"Beef has gotten cheap relative to pork over the past two weeks and that should entice some retail buying next week for mid-month features," said Dale Benson, analyst with Dean-Witter Reynolds in Chicago.
Boxed beef prices at midday Friday were up $0.30 to $0.76, with 105 loads sold, according to USDA.
